# Exact label-information retention of arbitrary quantum preparations

30 October 2026, Brisbane. Root's central construction, developed with C's
pure-frame extraction and B's independent modular reconstruction. Independent
whole-file challenge is pending. This is a supplied finite-channel theorem,
not physical channel acquisition or historical-priority clearance.

## 1. Operation and exact statement

Let n>=2 and let tau_1,...,tau_n be finite-dimensional density matrices.
The input label X is EXPLICITLY classical. The preparation channel sends
i to tau_i. For arbitrary finite quantum reference R and classical-quantum
hypotheses rho_XR,sigma_XR, define

 J_X=D(rho_XR||sigma_XR)-D(rho_R||sigma_R),
 J_tau=D((tau tensor id)rho||(tau tensor id)sigma)-D(rho_R||sigma_R).

Only defined finite differences are admitted. Let S be the support of
sum_j tau_j and let Pi_i project, WITHIN S, onto the kernel of
sum_(j!=i)tau_j. Set r_i=Tr(tau_i Pi_i), r=min_i r_i.

**Theorem.** For every admitted pair and every finite R,

    J_tau >= r J_X.                                      (1)

The constant r is SHARP, even restricting R to dimension1 and using
equal-reference hypotheses. Thus the sharp reverse factor is1/r if r>0,
and infinite if r=0. Equivalently,

 D_out >= r D_in+(1-r)D_reference.                        (2)

This does NOT follow merely from D_out>=rD_in. No classical-output
equal-reference/conditional equivalence is imported for these quantum
outputs. The changing-reference term is proved below.

For rational density matrices, kernel projectors, r_i and the sharp factor
are acquired by polynomial exact rational linear algebra. No optimization
over reference states, matrix logarithm or eigenvalue precision oracle is
needed for this operation. Exact supports are substantive input information.

## 2. The algebraic extraction identity

Assume first every r_i>0, and put E_i=Pi_i/r_i. On output Hilbert--Schmidt
space define T(Y)_i=Tr(E_iY), with adjoint T*e_i=E_i. This linear extraction
is NOT claimed to be a jointly normalized POVM.

# A finite rational witness below the exact reverse threshold

This construction makes the endpoint proof effective without a matrix-log
oracle. It uses the SAME supplied channel; no new channel, state search or
numerical case is acquired here. It is independently derived in this
challenge, with ownership separate from the producer's main theorem.

Let n>=2, choose a label i, and put

`B=(1/(n-1))sum_(j!=i) tau_j`,
`S=supp(B+tau_i)`, `P=projector ker(B) within S`,
`r=Tr tau_i P`.

All operators below are restricted to S. Take rational certified bounds

`0<a<=min(1,lambda_min(B+tau_i))`,
`0<b<=min(1,lambda_min^+(B))`.

These need no eigenvalue oracle for rational matrices: one may use
`a=min(1,1/Tr[(B+tau_i)^+])`,
`b=min(1,1/Tr[B^+])`, where + means the ordinary Moore--Penrose inverse
on the known exact support. The trace of an inverse is at least the
reciprocal of its smallest positive eigenvalue. Kernel bases and rational
orthogonal projectors give those pseudoinverses by rational elimination.

## 1. Uniform block lower bound

For `0<e<=ab/8`, define `B_e=(1-e)B+e tau_i`. Split S=P+Q with Q=I-P.
For vectors p in P and q in Q, use `||tau_i||<=1` and

`P tau_i P>=aP`, `QBQ>=bQ`.

Since e<=1/2,

`<(p,q),B_e(p,q)>
 >= e a||p||^2-2e||p||||q||+(b/2)||q||^2
 >= (e a/2)||p||^2+(b/2-2e/a)||q||^2
 >= (e a/2)||p||^2+(b/4)||q||^2`.                     (1)

The middle inequality is ordinary scalar Young. Thus, in operator order,

`B_e >= (e a/2)P+(b/4)Q`.                             (2)

This is also valid if P=0; no private-direction compression inverse was
used. Operator monotonicity of log, Tr(tau_i log tau_i)<=0, and (2) give

`D(tau_i||B_e)
 <= r log(1/e)+r log(2/a)+(1-r)log(4/b)
 <= r log(1/e)+log(8/(ab))`.                           (3)

All these relative entropies are finite: B_e is positive on the total
support S. If r=0, the formula still applies and supplies a finite
constant upper bound while the input divergence diverges.

## 2. A literal rational violating pair

Let c>=0 be any rational claimed reverse factor with `c r<1`. Compute
an integer h>=1 such that `2^h>=8/(ab)`, using integer comparisons only.
Put

`k=max(h, floor(c h/(1-c r))+1)`, `e=2^(-k)`.

The scalar-reference input hypotheses are

`p_i=1, p_j=0 (j!=i)`,
`q_i=e, q_j=(1-e)/(n-1) (j!=i)`.
